items.title: Served checklist rows carry a stale updated_at: work.py/store writes do not refresh the row's own updated_at, so /api/bot/work/checklist (SPA Work page) and every staleness reader show ages days too old

extra.note: Found 2026-11-12 ~08:00Z by UI lane p2. EVIDENCE: MANAGER-VM-DIRECT-OPS: store item updated_at 2026-11-12T01:16:46Z (Lane MANAGER-VM-DIRECT-OPS); GET /api/bot/work/checklist fields.updated_at 2026-11-05T00:46:28Z. Cause: work_store_import.to_row projects extra.updated_at (the row's own field), which only changes when the writer sets it; the store's item-level updated_at moves on every write. Effect: the SPA Work page's 'updated' ages, and any reader through work_read.checklist_rows (attention_watch, blocker_watch, work_digest, staleness checks), see rows days older than they are. FIX (5 lines, Tier 2 runtime read path): in work_read.checklist_rows (or to_row), take max(item.updated_at, extra.updated_at) and the matching updated_by. The console connector already does this client-side (PR #25164 data._fresh). CLOSES WHEN GET /api/bot/work/checklist shows MANAGER-VM-DIRECT-OPS updated_at equal to the store item's.

latest_note.note: #25569 merged 9cf7794c at ~01:25Z 2026-11-13 (Tier 2, manager standing OK, guards green). Write side: work_store._update stamps extra.updated_at/updated_by when the item carries one. Merged, not yet observed deployed. Closing observation: once ict-git-sync has the web-api on 9cf7794c or later, the next work.py write to any row shows the write time as that row's updated_at in GET /api/bot/work/checklist.

items.title: Frontier research: recurring weekly scan for BETTER models/methods (ML) and strategy ideas, not variations of the first good thing
items.terminal_reason: [2026-10-11 ~14:25Z operator directive, voice, close paraphrase] The ML research mandate must not be limited to new training runs, datasets or variations of models we already chose. Do deep research on BETTER MODELS: there is a vast and growing set of open-source models, methods and resources; stay on top of them, test whether they are relevant, and apply them. Do not let early, somewhat arbitrary choices dictate the scope and potential of the project; do not lazily keep the first good thing; do not spend capacity on 100 variations of the same model that is not going anywhere. Use capacity wisely to test genuinely different things. Same for strategies, but especially ML. RECURRING part of the workflow, alongside the work already under way.
